purpose: Current low-power edge AI mini PCs and Raspberry Pi-class GenAI expansion hardware relevant to local inference.
notes: Vendor TOPS figures are retained as vendor claims and are not treated as tokens/sec.
NPU support does not imply arbitrary GGUF/GPTQ/AWQ execution without a supported compiler/runtime path.
System power and accelerator power are kept distinct where sources provide only platform ratings.

quantization_compatibility: runtime-dependent ONNX/TensorRT-style or vendor-compiled paths; arbitrary GGUF not verified
hardware.model_size_practicality: Host-RAM dependent; suitable for small local assistants, speech/vision pipelines, embeddings, OCR and selected quantized models when supported by the runtime.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: moderate; compact platform with low-to-mid mobile-class power envelope, but complete-system measurements were not verified.
vendor_claims: AMD XDNA2 NPU delivers up to 55 AI TOPS.
Radeon 800M graphics support up to four 4K displays.

quantization_compatibility: runtime-dependent; no vendor claim of native GGUF execution verified
hardware.model_size_practicality: Host-memory dependent; best suited to small quantized models, RAG preprocessing, multimodal edge tasks and always-on assistants.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: moderate_to_high; very small chassis and 50-TOPS NPU positioning, but system wall-power data was not published.
vendor_claims: Up to 75% higher NPU performance than the previous generation.

host_requirements: Raspberry Pi OS / supported Linux stack
quantization_compatibility: vendor-supported compiled GenAI models; model support is runtime/artifact dependent
hardware.model_size_practicality: Small local GenAI and multimodal workloads; Raspberry Pi host memory and Hailo model support constrain larger models.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: very_high; approximately 3 W add-on board power claim, excluding Raspberry Pi 5 and peripherals.
vendor_claims: Designed to run generative AI models locally on Raspberry Pi 5.
